data_fields.name: follow_gain_per_call
data_fields.donor_constant: 0.85 of the gap per call (frame-rate dependent; not copied)

data_fields.name: follow_half_life_s
data_fields.donor_constant: not in donor; proposed 0.08 s, time-based ease

data_fields.name: free_look_return_s
data_fields.donor_constant: not in donor; proposed 0.5 s to return to the hero

best_idea: Keep one camera target that the hero writes each frame unless free look is on, let free look pan that same target, and always ease the camera toward it.
decision_why: The shared target, the free-look gate and the pan-the-target rule give manual look and auto-follow one code path for the world camera; the per-call 0.85 gain is frame-rate dependent and the one-frame target delay adds lag, so both are rejected.
acceptance: With the hero walking at a steady speed the camera trails by the same distance at 30 and 60 fps; holding the free-look key pans the view and releasing it returns to the hero within 0.5 s; the pan never changes the hero's position. A client test asserts the trailing distance agrees at 30 and 60 fps and that the pan leaves server state unchanged.
